QuestionText: Work is done when:
Options: A) A force acts on an object
B) A force acts and displacement occurs in the direction of force
C) An object is at rest
Explanation: W = Fd cosθ. Work is done only when force causes displacement. If displacement is zero (pushing a wall) or force is perpendicular to displacement, work = 0.

QuestionText: SI unit of work and energy is:
Explanation: 1 Joule = 1 Newton × 1 metre. Work and energy both measured in Joules.

QuestionText: Work done = ?
Explanation: W = F × d (when force and displacement are in same direction). More generally: W = Fd cosθ.

QuestionText: Kinetic energy of a moving object is:
Explanation: KE = ½mv². Depends on mass and square of speed. Always positive.

QuestionText: Potential energy due to position in a gravitational field is:
Explanation: Gravitational PE = mgh. Depends on mass, g, and height above reference level.

QuestionText: Law of conservation of energy states:
Options: A) Energy is created by machines
B) Total energy remains constant; can only be converted
C) Mechanical energy is always conserved
Explanation: Energy can neither be created nor destroyed; it can only be converted from one form to another. Total energy of a closed system is constant.

QuestionText: Power is defined as:
Explanation: Power P = Work/Time = Energy/Time. SI unit: Watt (W). 1 W = 1 J/s.

QuestionText: A machine does 600 J of work in 30s. Its power is:
Work-Energy Theorem states:
Options: B) Net work done = change in kinetic energy
Explanation: W_net = ΔKE = ½mv² - ½mu². Net work changes the kinetic energy of an object.

QuestionText: A person lifts a 10 kg object to height 3m (g=10). Work done = ?
KE of 4 kg object moving at 5 m/s = ?
Explanation: KE = ½mv² = ½×4×25 = 50 J.

QuestionText: If speed is doubled, kinetic energy becomes:
Explanation: KE ∝ v². If v doubles: KE = ½m(2v)² = 4(½mv²). Kinetic energy quadruples.

QuestionText: At maximum height, a projectile's PE is maximum and KE is:
Explanation: At max height: KE = 0 (for vertical throw) and PE = maximum. Total mechanical energy is conserved (if no friction).

QuestionText: 1 horse power (HP) = ?
Explanation: 1 HP = 746 W. Old unit of power named after horsepower. 1 kW = 1000 W.

QuestionText: Commercial unit of energy is:
Explanation: 1 kWh = 1 unit of electricity = 3.6 × 10⁶ J. Used in electricity bills. 1 kWh = 1000 W × 3600 s.

QuestionText: 1 kWh = ?
Work done by friction is always:
Explanation: Friction opposes motion → acts opposite to displacement → W = Fd cos180° = -Fd. Always negative.

QuestionText: A ball of mass 2 kg falls from rest from 10m height. KE just before hitting ground (g=10) = ?
Explanation: All PE converts to KE. KE = PE = mgh = 2×10×10 = 200 J.

QuestionText: Gravitational PE is measured with respect to a:
Explanation: PE is measured relative to a chosen reference level (usually ground). PE can be positive or negative depending on choice.

QuestionText: A machine with power 5000 W does work for 2 minutes. Work done = ?
If you push a wall and it doesn't move, work done = ?
Explanation: Work = Force × displacement. If wall doesn't move: displacement = 0 → W = 0.

QuestionText: Energy stored in a stretched spring is:
Explanation: Elastic PE = ½kx² stored in stretched/compressed spring. Released as KE when spring returns to natural length.

QuestionText: Total mechanical energy = ?
Explanation: Total mechanical energy = KE + PE. In absence of friction, this is conserved (constant throughout motion).

QuestionText: A boy of mass 40 kg runs up a flight of stairs of height 5m in 10s (g=10). Power generated = ?
Which form of energy is released when wood is burned?
Explanation: Wood stores chemical energy. Burning converts it to heat and light energy.

QuestionText: A pendulum at one extreme has maximum:
Explanation: At the extreme positions, pendulum momentarily stops (v=0, KE=0). All energy is PE (maximum height).

QuestionText: At the mean position, pendulum has maximum:
Explanation: At mean position (lowest point), height=minimum (PE=minimum), speed=maximum → KE = maximum.

QuestionText: Work done when force is perpendicular to displacement (θ=90°) = ?
Explanation: W = Fd cos90° = 0. Centripetal force does no work on circular orbit. Normal force does no work on horizontal motion.

QuestionText: A 2 kg ball moving at 10 m/s has KE = ?
Solar panels convert __ energy to __ energy.
Explanation: Solar cells/panels use photoelectric effect to convert light (solar) energy directly into electrical energy.

QuestionText: Which is NOT a renewable source of energy?
Explanation: Coal is a fossil fuel — non-renewable. Solar, wind, and hydro are renewable (naturally replenished).

QuestionText: The efficiency of a machine is:
Explanation: Efficiency = (useful output energy / total input energy) × 100%. Real machines have efficiency < 100% due to friction losses.

QuestionText: An electric bulb uses 60 W for 5 hours. Energy consumed (in kWh) = ?
Explanation: Energy = Power × Time = 60W × 5h = 300 Wh = 0.3 kWh.

QuestionText: An elevator motor lifts 500 kg through 10m in 20s (g=10). Power of motor = ?
When a car brakes, kinetic energy converts mainly to:
Explanation: Friction between brake pads and disc converts KE to heat. Regenerative braking (in EVs) converts some to electrical energy.

QuestionText: Energy can be measured in:
Explanation: Energy can be expressed in Joules (SI), kWh (commercial), Calories (food/nutrition), BTU (British). All are units of energy.

QuestionText: If work done against gravity = 500 J, PE gained = ?
Explanation: Work done against gravity = PE gained. Energy is stored as gravitational PE.

QuestionText: Watt-second equals:
Explanation: 1 Watt-second = 1 J (since 1 W = 1 J/s). Power × time = energy.

QuestionText: A body of mass m falls freely from height h. Just before hitting ground, v = ?
Explanation: PE = KE: mgh = ½mv² → v = √(2gh). Mass cancels.

QuestionText: Nuclear energy is energy stored in:
Explanation: Nuclear energy is released from the nucleus (fission or fusion). Enormous energy (E=mc²).

QuestionText: Negative work is done when:
Options: A) Force and displacement are parallel
B) Force and displacement are anti-parallel (opposite directions)
Explanation: W = Fd cosθ. When θ=180°: W = -Fd. Friction does negative work. Brakes do negative work.

QuestionText: A hydroelectric power station converts:
Options: B) Gravitational PE of water to electrical
Explanation: Hydroelectric: water flows down (PE → KE) → turns turbines → generates electricity. Clean, renewable energy.

QuestionText: KE of a 5 kg object at 4 m/s equals PE at height h (g=10). Find h.
What is the work done in moving a 20 N force over 4 m at 60° to displacement?
The energy transformation in a microphone is:
Explanation: Microphone: sound (mechanical) → electrical signal. Speaker: electrical → sound. Both are transducers.

QuestionText: A 100 W bulb and a 40 W bulb both run for 1 hour. Total energy consumed = ?
Explanation: Total energy = (100+40)×1 = 140 Wh = 0.14 kWh.

QuestionText: In an ideal (no friction) pendulum, total mechanical energy:
Explanation: Without friction: KE + PE = constant at all positions. Energy just converts between KE and PE forms.

QuestionText: Work done in pulling a 10 kg block 5m along frictionless floor with F=50N (horizontal) is:
Explanation: W=F×d=50×5=250 J (force and displacement are parallel, θ=0°, cos0°=1).

QuestionText: Which has more KE: 2 kg at 4 m/s or 4 kg at 2 m/s?
Explanation: KE₁=½×2×16=16 J. KE₂=½×4×4=8 J. First object has more KE.

QuestionText: A motor lifts 200 kg water to a tank 10m above in 5 minutes (g=10). Power = ?
